questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Close to home, and the history of the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Made many friends along the way.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The important information was sent over mail, with deadlines etc. The university site had all information i needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation day with guided tour of campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would reccomend Erasmus in Prague.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure it is a legit booking site/company, so you don't get scammed, but private renting might be cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A bit complex to understand, the final course-registration was first done after the first few weeks of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office and coordinator was available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, i could almost choose any course i wanted from the science faculty.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't decide on final courses before arrival, to obtain the 30 ECTS you need several courses and plan your own schedule after each course schedule announced. Search "alternative courses" like sport, fieldtrips etc. in good time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found it at the correct level for a BA student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less syllabus readings, primarily syllabus presented at lectures. Some courses had one text and a little essay text to do each week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Introduction to Polar Ecology
- Ecology, History, Myth
- Flood Risk Management
- Remote sensing in Physical Geography
- Heritage of Cultural Landscapes
- Exploring contemporary migration trends: Diasporas, Refugees and Environmental migration
- Urban Social Geography: Key Theoretical Approaches

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
"Remote sensing in Physical Geography" is a good if you have knowlegde in remote sensing. Work in ESA SNAP is done during exercises. 
"Heritage of Cultural Landscapes" did not have any readings or homework. 
"Flood Risk Management" is a good course about Czech flood risks from rivers and flood risk in general.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Generally cheaper living costs. 
I had to pay rent i cash, the withdrawal fee at atm was not high, but unexpected for rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Science club for science students. A lot of different sports activities. 
And dancing, food and hiking for Erasmus/science students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many visit other cities and historic monuments nearby Prague. Since it is cheap to travel from there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Found it very easy, since i lived with two people i knew from home.
Though i begin seeing it as home by the end of the trip.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and talk to people from different backgrounds.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the language, since a lot of people weren't fluent in english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The nightlife, and cheap food.
Especially Vietnamese/Asian-fusion is good and cheap.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not try to have all the courses and registration done before you start - they will guide you through it. 
Accept that the beginning of the semester is a bit confusing - you will most likely need to change you pre-approval fx. 
Book housing early - the university dorms are cheap, but a bit far from the city center.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure the courses you sign up for is fitting with your academic level and direction.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people i got to know from other Erasmus countries, and the cultural experiences we got together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of different courses was a bit overwhelming compared to home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
